sa28:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa28:2.1: There was then a certain monk who came to visit the Buddha.
sa28:2.2: He bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to stand at one side, and said to the Buddha,
sa28:2.3: “Bhagavān, the Bhagavān says ‘attain nirvāṇa in the present life.’
sa28:2.4: How does a monk attain nirvāṇa in the present life?”
sa28:3.2: “Good, good! Do you want now to know about nirvāṇa in the present life?”
sa28:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa28:5.2: “[Listen closely!] Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa28:5.3: I will explain it for you.”
sa28:6.2: “Becoming disillusioned with form, becoming free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it, the contaminants don’t arise, and the mind is properly liberated.
sa28:6.3: This is called a monk who attains nirvāṇa in the present life.
sa28:6.4: It’s the same with feeling, conception, volition, and awareness … becoming disillusioned with awareness, becoming free of desire for it, and completely ceasing it, the contaminants don’t arise, and the mind is properly liberated.
sa28:6.5: This is called a monk who attains nirvāṇa in the present life.”
sa28:7.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he celebrated and rejoiced.
